Dying Light 2 is one of my favorite games. An absolute masterpiece. The characters are memorable, and the world looks awesome. Villedor’s environment offers so much variety that exploring never feels dull. The parkour is one of the best parts of Dying Light 2. The best parkour mechanics in the entire Dying Light series is definitely in Dying Light 2. That’s because the variety of spots and moves is unbelievable. You can mix up different parkour styles and moves almost anywhere you go. Moving through the city feels very smooth and satisfying.

I also enjoyed the Tower Raid experience. it added variety to the gameplay. Personally, I find the story stronger than the first game, especially because of the characters and world design. The many activities, locations, enemies, and ways to approach situations keep every playthrough fresh. After 100 hours and five playthroughs, I am still coming back for more.

Even after the story is done there's still several different side missions, multiple Easter Eggs (including a pixelated DOOM event), countless community-made maps, a tower raid mode that can be repeated endlessly, no real end to personal progress (even after you're fully upgraded you then have "legend" levels that allow even more upgrades), and of course an endless amount of targets to satisfy your bloodlust.

And if you don't want to slaughter people with melee weapons you can use the recently added guns. 
Don't complain that you can't use them immediately, as the game wasn't built for them.

# Dying Light 2: Stay Human

### "Humanity is dying. At least the parkour is alive."

**Recommended. Absolutely worth the fall.**

The world ended, civilization collapsed, and humanity somehow decided that living on rooftops was a reasonable career choice.

Welcome to Villedor.

Dying Light 2 takes everything that made the first game fun and throws you into a massive open world where every rooftop is a playground, every building is a shortcut, and every wrong turn can become a one-way trip to the ground floor.

The parkour feels incredible. Gliding across rooftops, swinging between buildings, and barely surviving a fall you definitely should not have survived never gets old. Combat is brutal, weapons break, infected swarm the streets, and sometimes the best strategy is to run like you've got 47 unpaid bills chasing you.

And then there's nighttime.

The streets become a death sentence, infected become nightmares with legs, and suddenly that tiny UV light looks more valuable than your entire inventory. You can spend the whole day feeling like an unstoppable badass, only to spend the night screaming internally while running for your life.

The story has its ups and downs, and not every choice hits as hard as it should. But the atmosphere, exploration, movement, and sheer chaos of surviving in Villedor make it ridiculously easy to lose hours in this world.

Is it perfect? No.

Does it always reach the same level of horror as the first game? Not quite.

But when you're flying off a skyscraper, deploying your paraglider at the last possible second, landing on a rooftop, and immediately dropkicking an infected into the next dimension, you remember exactly why you bought this game.

**Dying Light 2 isn't just about staying human. It's about losing 30 minutes of your life because you saw a cool rooftop and forgot you had actual missions to complete.**

**9/10 — The world may be falling apart, but I'm still hitting every rooftop like I own the place.**

*Keep moving. Trust nobody. And for the love of God, get inside before sunset.*

The Review

Dying Light 2 is one of those games that took me a while to fully appreciate. The story and characters can be hit or miss, and some of the dialogue feels a little cheesy, but once you get into the parkour and combat, the game becomes seriously fun.

The parkour is easily the best part. Running across rooftops, jumping between buildings, and escaping a horde of infected never really gets old. The nighttime sections are also genuinely tense, especially when you’re underleveled and suddenly realize you’ve got way more zombies chasing you than you can handle.

The combat feels good once you unlock more skills and get better gear, and there’s a decent amount of freedom in how you approach situations. The world itself is also fun to explore, with plenty of random encounters, side activities, and things to discover.

The Reloaded Edition is a great package if you’re starting fresh, especially with the extra content and improvements that have been added since launch. That said, the game still has some bugs and occasional jank, and the story definitely isn't going to be the main reason you keep playing.

Overall, it's a really fun open-world zombie game with fantastic movement, satisfying combat, and a surprisingly addictive gameplay loop.

8/10 — If you like zombies, parkour, and exploring open worlds, definitely worth picking up.

First off its not nearly as dark so the atmosphere is already way less scary and volatiles in this game just overall arent very intimidating, I found myself getting more angry dealing with them than scared, since they completely make you unable to move your screen when hitting you and they just sometimes decide to completely ignore the uv light and molly whop you 3 times and youre just dead.

Volatile "nests" are also just laughably garbage compared to the first game aswell, in dying light 1 the nests were huge with a ton of zombies and body piles and gore everywhere and really blood gorey etc, in this game its just a random fucking volatile half way in the ground with like 2 of them protecting it in some random building... fucking pathetic. The guns in this game are way too overpowered, basically the only downside is attracting virals which doesnt even matter 90% of the time. In the lore its talked about how ammo is super rare and scarce but you can buy it infinitely and even find it on zombies? really dont understand that lol. The grappling hook was eviscerated in this game, I can admit it was super overpowered in the first game, parkour basically became redundant once you got it, but in this game it just turned into a fucking tarzan rope swing which you almost never use, besides main story locations giving you the perfect areas to use it, or just using a tech to scale a building with no parkour which makes the nerf basically pointless. Every gre anomaly is just the exact same with more health dependent on the tier, more laziness. The dlc is also mostly uninteresting, it makes it sound like its some gladiator arena dlc where u constantly fight people but its not, you fight people maybe like... once or twice, then youre just completing mostly unfun challenges though to be fair some of them were pretty cool, until you get the rank behind the final boss then youre actually put into the arena, and surprise surprise the final boss is a complete pushover, the store page rating of it is accurate. 

OK the last thing I wanna talk about is the achievements. Most of them are fine but holy shit there are some that are just so braindead that I do not understand how a developer decided to keep it as is. The save 50 people achievement is cancer, theres about 6 different variations of the blue diamond marker and I believe only 2 of them count towards the achievement, If you get unlucky and its not one of those 2 have fun wandering around for about 5 minutes testing your luck again about 50 times, afaik there is no way to manipulate the odds in this game unlike the first one. Every single collectible achievement besides the graffiti are utter bullshit, there are some you literally cannot get anymore if you progress too far without completing a random side quest, unless youre just following a guide prior youre fucked unless you wanna replay the game 2-3 times. Over 100 hours and I just decided to sam the achievement, I am not doing this legit.

Overall very mid game that is mostly just worse than the first game, but I think it is still worth playing if youre a fan of the series, I would rate this game as a neutral rating, but that does not exist so I will be voting it as not recommended.
